RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 20

Panel composition alone is not evidence. All-women panels occur routinely by chance in many departments, and research on academic hiring shows no consistent bias from same-sex panels — in some experiments women evaluators favour male candidates. Raising it would signal grievance rather than substance and would likely cost you credibility in a small field.

Your stronger ground is procedural: an unanswered request for written reasons. At a public university you may have a statutory right to the decision and its basis. Send a dated follow-up to the HR head or registrar, cite your original request, and ask whether the published criteria weighted industry experience above research and teaching.

If the stated criteria don't match the outcome, that's your case — not the panel's sex.
